subject: Nimble just samples some parameters for parametric weighted stochastic block model.

messages.author: f9c38c48fb29f7c3
messages.subject: Nimble just samples some parameters for parametric weighted stochastic block model.
parts:
Hello to everyone!

I created a relatively simple code implementing a parametric weighted stochastic block model to kind of play around and get familiar with Nimble. The model code is the following
```
model_code_param_ext <- nimbleCode({
 
  ## Prior for probability for vertices to be in blocks
  r[1:nB] ~ ddirch(pc[1:nB])
 
  ## Prior for connectivity within blocks + edges parameter distr.
  for (a in 1:nB){
    for (b in 1:nB){
      B[a,b] ~ dbeta(beta1, beta2)
      ## We assume same hyperparameters for shapes and rates.
      shapes[a,b] ~ dgamma(nu, beta)
      rates[a,b] ~ dgamma(nu, beta)
    }
  }
 
  ###### Vertex block membership
  for (i in 1:N){
    Z[i] ~ dcat(r[1:nB])
  }
 
  ##### Now we go to the likelihood of the adiecency matrix and of the weights.
  for (i in 1:N){
    for(j in 1:N){
    #for(j in 1:i-1){
      A[i,j] ~ dbinom(size=1, prob=B[Z[i], Z[j]])
      W[i,j] ~ dweigthbm_gamma(shapes[Z[i], Z[j]], rates[Z[i], Z[j]], A[i,j])
    }
  }
})
```

with `dweigthbm_gamma`
```
dweigthbm_gamma <- nimbleFunction(
  run=function(x=double(0), shape_ij=double(0), rate_ij=double(0), A_ij=integer(0), log=integer(0, default=0)){
    returnType(double(0))
    if (A_ij != 0){
      val <- dgamma(x, shape=shape_ij, rate=rate_ij)
    }
    else{
      if (x != 0){
        val <- 0.0
      }
      else{
        val <- 1.0
      }
    }
    if (log) return(log(val))
    else return(log)
  }
)

rweigthbm_gamma <- nimbleFunction(
  run=function(n=integer(0,default=1), shape_ij=double(0), rate_ij=double(0), A_ij=integer(0)){
    returnType(double(0))
    if (A_ij != 0){
      return (rgamma(n=1, shape=shape_ij, rate=rate_ij))
    }
    else{
      return(0)
    }
  }
)
 ```

I then create a slightly misspecified dataset to test the sample in the following way:
```
K <- 2
## Number of blocks
nB <- 2
## Number of vertices in the graph
n <- 50

B = matrix(0,nrow=nB, ncol=nB)
B[1,1] = 0.5
B[2,2] = 0.7
B[1,2] = 0.2
B[2,1] = B[1,2]
shapes <- array(c(100.0,50.0))
rates <- array(c(100.0, 10.0))

pi_0 <- array(c(0.75, 0.25))
pi_1 <- array(c(0.25, 0.75))

## Generate the data according to the model
Z_true = array(0, n)
for (i in 1:n){
  Z_true[i] = rcat(prob=r)
}

A = matrix(0, nrow=n, ncol=n)
W = matrix(0, nrow=n, ncol=n)
s_true = matrix(nrow=n, ncol=n)


for (i in 2:n){
  for (j in 1:(i-1)){
    if (Z_true[i]==Z_true[j]){
      s_true[i,j] = rcat(prob=pi_0)
      s_true[j,i] = s_true[i,j]
    }
    else{
      s_true[i,j] = rcat(prob=pi_1)
      s_true[j,i] = s_true[i,j]
    }
    A[i,j] = rbinom(n=1, size=1, prob=B[Z_true[i], Z_true[j]])
    A[j,i] = A[i,j]
    if (A[i,j] == 1){
      W[i,j] = rgamma(n=1, shape=shapes[s_true[i,j]], rate=rates[s_true[i,j]])
      W[j,i] = W[i,j]
    }
  }
}
```

where the misspecification is in the weights. I then compile the model and sample
```
pc <- 3 * array(1, dim=c(nB))

## Seem to give diffuse enough priors
nu <- 10
beta <- 4
beta1 <- 1.5
beta2 <- 1.5

data_pext = list(A=A, W=W)
constants_pext = list(N=n, nB=nB, pc=pc , nu=nu, beta=beta, beta1=beta1, beta2=beta2)
Rmodel_param <- nimbleModel(code=model_code_param_ext, constants = constants_pext, data=data_pext)
conf_param <- configureMCMC(Rmodel_param, monitors=c("Z", "B", "shapes", "rates", "r"))
Rmcmc_param <- buildMCMC(conf_param)
Cmodel_param <- compileNimble(Rmodel_param)
Cmcmc_param <- compileNimble(Rmcmc_param, project = Rmodel_param)

mcmc.out_param <- runMCMC(Cmcmc_param, niter=2000, nburnin=0, nchains=1, summary=TRUE)
```

During the sampling I get no error messages/warnings, and when I look at the output I get:
```
                  Mean    Median    St.Dev. 95%CI_low 95%CI_upp
B[1, 1]      0.3757850 0.3725258 0.01902426 0.3456662 0.4180413
B[2, 1]      0.4485430 0.4367798 0.11018092 0.2109650 0.7865345
B[1, 2]      0.4477253 0.4370324 0.11126312 0.2121075 0.8060270
B[2, 2]      0.6186998 0.6378723 0.14178728 0.1740158 0.8263060
Z[1]         1.8010000 2.0000000 0.39934789 1.0000000 2.0000000
Z[2]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[3]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[4]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[5]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[6]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[7]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[8]         1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[9]         1.8050000 2.0000000 0.39629979 1.0000000 2.0000000
Z[10]        1.8115000 2.0000000 0.39120873 1.0000000 2.0000000
Z[11]        1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[12]        1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
Z[13]        1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
......
......
```

Hence most of the latent variables have not moved during the sampling, which seems very very odd. Does anyone have an idea of what could cause this behaviour?

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Nimble just samples some parameters for parametric weighted stochastic block model.
parts:
Hi Luca,

A couple thoughts on how to investigate further:

1) Check the posterior for `r` -- does it collapse to putting all its mass on one element?

2) If not, try to see whether other values of Z[i] are reasonable for a given i. In particular, consider one of the Z[i]'s that is always equal to one in the MCMC. After running the MCMC for a bit,  try changing that Z[i] to the various other possible values in the compiled model and see what the result of compiled_model$calculate() is.  Possibly for some reason, all the other values give terrible model log probability values. If so try to see what part of the model is preventing Z[i] from being some other value. Note that by default, the sampler for a `dcat` node should calculate the log probability for all possible values of Z[i] and choose from amongst the possible values based on that log probability - i.e., a conjugate sampler in the discrete space.

-chris

messages.subject: Re: Nimble just samples some parameters for parametric weighted stochastic block model.
parts:
So I did try to implement some of the suggestion you where mentioning, but none of them solve the problem. 

The posterior values for the variable 'r', although not centeredat the true ones, are not at any degenerate value ether. They are just wrong. Also, looking at one of the frozen variables it does not seem that the other value would have been "terrible". I also considered this option and kind of though of a theoretical reasoning for it, but then looking at the values this is not the case. 

To give an example here is a flip of the frozen variable:

> Cmodel_param$getLogProb("Z[1]")
[1] -0.2306881
> Cmodel_param$Z[1] ### value was 2
[1] 2
> Cmodel_param$Z[1]<-1
> Cmodel_param$Z[1]
[1] 1
> Cmodel_param$calculate()
[1] -4222.443
> Cmodel_param$getLogProb("Z[1]")
[1] -1.579816
> exp(-0.2306881)
[1] 0.7939871
> exp(-1.579816)
[1] 0.206013

So from the output it does not seem to be a case where "Z[1]| rest of params" is a sort of dirac. Is there a way to see the proposal of the algorithm at the different steps? Or to kind of implement step by step its sample generation mechanism to see where the bug(I think after this evidence it has to be a bug) could be? 

Best,
Luca

messages.subject: Re: Nimble just samples some parameters for parametric weighted stochastic block model.
parts:
Hi Luca,

1) You can run the MCMC uncompiled and use R's debugger to try to figure out what is going on. Here's a basic example:

code <- nimbleCode({
    y ~ dnorm(mu, sd = sigma)
    mu ~ dnorm(0,1)
    sigma ~ dunif(0,10)
})
m <- nimbleModel(code, data = list(y=1))
mcmc <- buildMCMC(m)
debug(mcmc$samplerFunctions[[2]]$run)  # debug sigma sampler
mcmc$run(10)

In your case, if you do

debug(Rmcmc_param$samplerFunctions[[14]]$run)
Rmcmc_param$run(10)

that should put you into debugging mode in the sampler for the first Z.

2) I'm trying this out for your model to see what I notice. I am seeing that at a given iteration one of the two possible values for a given Z[i] has much higher probability in the cases I am looking at. This seems mainly caused by the logProb for the dependent W nodes (and to a lesser extent the dependent A nodes) rather than by the (prior) logProb for the Z[i] node being sampled. So from what I am seeing the model gets stuck on a given value for Z[i] because the density of dependent nodes is much lower if it tries to change the value of Z[i]. 

I'm happy to continue this discussion -- perhaps you can try the debugging approach above and try to see if you also see what I am describing above during the MCMC sampling and if you can understand why the density for the dependent nodes under a given value for Z[i] is much lower than for the alternative value of Z[i]. 

For further discussion, please make sure that you set `r` in your code (currently in the code in your email it is not set) and that you set a random number seed so that I can run exactly the code you are running and get the same results.

-chris

Also, looking at one of the frozen variables it does not seem that the other value would have been "terrible". Best,

Il giorno sabato 28 ottobre 2023 alle 12:38:35 UTC-4 Chris Paciorek ha scritto:
Hi Luca,

A couple thoughts on how to investigate further:

1) Check the posterior for `r` -- does it collapse to putting all its mass on one element?

2) If not, try to see whether other values of Z[i] are reasonable for a given i. In particular, consider one of the Z[i]'s that is always equal to one in the MCMC. After running the MCMC for a bit,  try changing that Z[i] to the various other possible values in the compiled model and see what the result of compiled_model$calculate() is.  Possibly for some reason, all the other values give terrible model log probability values. If so try to see what part of the model is preventing Z[i] from being some other value. Note that by default, the sampler for a `dcat` node should calculate the log probability for all possible values of Z[i] and choose from amongst the possible values based on that log probability - i.e., a conjugate sampler in the discrete space.

-chris

Hello to everyone!

I created a relatively simple code implementing a parametric weighted stochastic block model to kind of play around and get familiar with Nimble. The model code is the following
```
model_code_param_ext <- nimbleCode({
 
  ## Prior for probability for vertices to be in blocks
  r[1:nB] ~ ddirch(pc[1:nB])
 
  ## Prior for connectivity within blocks + edges parameter distr.
  for (a in 1:nB){
    for (b in 1:nB){
      B[a,b] ~ dbeta(beta1, beta2)
      ## We assume same hyperparameters for shapes and rates.
      shapes[a,b] ~ dgamma(nu, beta)
      rates[a,b] ~ dgamma(nu, beta)
    }
  }
 
  ###### Vertex block membership
  for (i in 1:N){
    Z[i] ~ dcat(r[1:nB])
  }
 
  ##### Now we go to the likelihood of the adiecency matrix and of the weights.
  for (i in 1:N){
    for(j in 1:N){
    #for(j in 1:i-1){
      A[i,j] ~ dbinom(size=1, prob=B[Z[i], Z[j]])
      W[i,j] ~ dweigthbm_gamma(shapes[Z[i], Z[j]], rates[Z[i], Z[j]], A[i,j])
    }
  }
})
```

with `dweigthbm_gamma`
```
dweigthbm_gamma <- nimbleFunction(
  run=function(x=double(0), shape_ij=double(0), rate_ij=double(0), A_ij=integer(0), log=integer(0, default=0)){
    returnType(double(0))
    if (A_ij != 0){
      val <- dgamma(x, shape=shape_ij, rate=rate_ij)
    }
    else{
      if (x != 0){
        val <- 0.0
      }
      else{
        val <- 1.0
      }
    }
    if (log) return(log(val))
    else return(log)
  }
)

rweigthbm_gamma <- nimbleFunction(
  run=function(n=integer(0,default=1), shape_ij=double(0), rate_ij=double(0), A_ij=integer(0)){
    returnType(double(0))
    if (A_ij != 0){
      return (rgamma(n=1, shape=shape_ij, rate=rate_ij))
    }
    else{
      return(0)
    }
  }
)
 ```

I then create a slightly misspecified dataset to test the sample in the following way:
```
K <- 2
## Number of blocks
nB <- 2
## Number of vertices in the graph
n <- 50

B = matrix(0,nrow=nB, ncol=nB)
B[1,1] = 0.5
B[2,2] = 0.7
B[1,2] = 0.2
B[2,1] = B[1,2]
shapes <- array(c(100.0,50.0))
rates <- array(c(100.0, 10.0))

pi_0 <- array(c(0.75, 0.25))
pi_1 <- array(c(0.25, 0.75))

## Generate the data according to the model
Z_true = array(0, n)
for (i in 1:n){
  Z_true[i] = rcat(prob=r)
}

A = matrix(0, nrow=n, ncol=n)
W = matrix(0, nrow=n, ncol=n)
s_true = matrix(nrow=n, ncol=n)


for (i in 2:n){
  for (j in 1:(i-1)){
    if (Z_true[i]==Z_true[j]){
      s_true[i,j] = rcat(prob=pi_0)
      s_true[j,i] = s_true[i,j]
    }
    else{
      s_true[i,j] = rcat(prob=pi_1)
      s_true[j,i] = s_true[i,j]
    }
    A[i,j] = rbinom(n=1, size=1, prob=B[Z_true[i], Z_true[j]])
    A[j,i] = A[i,j]
    if (A[i,j] == 1){
      W[i,j] = rgamma(n=1, shape=shapes[s_true[i,j]], rate=rates[s_true[i,j]])
      W[j,i] = W[i,j]
    }
  }
}
```

where the misspecification is in the weights. I then compile the model and sample
```
pc <- 3 * array(1, dim=c(nB))

## Seem to give diffuse enough priors
nu <- 10
beta <- 4
beta1 <- 1.5
beta2 <- 1.5

data_pext = list(A=A, W=W)
constants_pext = list(N=n, nB=nB, pc=pc , nu=nu, beta=beta, beta1=beta1, beta2=beta2)
Rmodel_param <- nimbleModel(code=model_code_param_ext, constants = constants_pext, data=data_pext)
conf_param <- configureMCMC(Rmodel_param, monitors=c("Z", "B", "shapes", "rates", "r"))
Rmcmc_param <- buildMCMC(conf_param)
Cmodel_param <- compileNimble(Rmodel_param)
Cmcmc_param <- compileNimble(Rmcmc_param, project = Rmodel_param)

mcmc.out_param <- runMCMC(Cmcmc_param, niter=2000, nburnin=0, nchains=1, summary=TRUE)
```

During the sampling I get no error messages/warnings, and when I look at the output I get:
```
